title: ADLAI corpus export contract (STORY-100)
description: Contract for the JSON files this repo exports under output/<slug>.json. Validated by scripts/lint_corpus_contract.js (npm run lint:corpus). `law_type` is now a real per-entry field (added 2026-09), stamped from the same 8 law_type -> slug(s) DOMAIN_MAP already used by scripts/verify_prd_gate.js -- previously derived from the filename only, but ADLAI's contract of record requires it present on every record, so it's now written into the data itself and required below. `chunk_hash` (2026-09): per the release contract, this is tracked internally only and must NOT appear in the exported release files -- removed from every output/*.json record and now explicitly disallowed here (see the `not` clause below), settling the earlier back-and-forth over whether it was required or forbidden.

law_type.description: One of the 8 domain groupings (ZATCA, PDPL, SAMA, CMA, NCA, MISA, COMPANIES, LABOR) -- see DOMAIN_MAP in scripts/lint_corpus_contract.js.

article_number.description: Integer (or integer.5 for an inserted 'mکرر' article, e.g. CMA's 20.5) article number, or null for documents with no legal article numbering (e.g. NCA's ECC/CCC controls, which use section_ref instead).

section_ref.description: Hierarchical citable reference for non-article documents (e.g. 'ecc:1-1-1', 'ccc:1-1-م-1-1'). Required and must be non-empty whenever article_number is null (see the if/then below) -- this is the STORY-100 Phase 2 rule: 'no null article numbers without a populated section_ref'.

language.description: 'ar' or 'en'. Combined 'ar,en' bilingual entries (misa, sama_banking_control_law) were split into two single-language records each in 2026-09, per ADLAI's request for one encoding across the export -- no longer a valid value here, so it's no longer accepted.

source_url.description: Some real source URLs (labor.json, sama_*) contain raw (non-percent-encoded) Arabic characters copied straight from a browser address bar. ajv-formats' 'uri' format enforces strict RFC 3986 (would reject those as invalid), and it has no 'iri' format to fall back on -- so this just checks for an http(s):// scheme instead of using a format keyword.

fetched_at.description: Not required: null/absent for misa, sama_banking_control_law, sama_central_bank_law today -- a real, pre-existing gap (see lint output), not something this schema should paper over by inventing a timestamp.
